bug_description: tf.keras.layers.ZeroPadding3D with an extremely large padding value (1610612736) crashes the TensorFlow process with SIGSEGV when executed through tf.function(jit_compile=True) on CPU. The padding value 1610612736 (0x60000000) causes the output spatial dimensions to overflow (input_dim + 2 * padding overflows int32/int64 shape representation). During XLA compilation the overflowed shape propagates into buffer planning or memory allocation, leading to a segmentation fault in the native C++ execution path. The crash is not raised as a Python exception — the process is killed by signal 11 (SIGSEGV).

build() {

}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/tensorflow
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"
    case "$command" in
        build) build "$@" ;;
        repro) repro "$@" ;;
        patch) patch "$@" ;;
        *) echo "Unknown command: $command"; echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi

bug_report:
================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/116716
## Description:
Issue: tensorflow/tensorflow#116716
Title: SIGSEGV when compiling tf.keras.layers.ZeroPadding3D with extremely large padding under XLA
State: open
Labels: type:bug, comp:xla, 2.21.0
Created at: 2026-04

Issue Body:
tf.keras.layers.ZeroPadding3D with an extremely large padding value can crash the TensorFlow worker process with SIGSEGV when executed through tf.function(jit_compile=True) on CPU.

The failure is not raised as a Python exception. Instead, the subprocess exits with signal 11:

worker died by SIGSEGV
exitcode: -11

This suggests a native runtime crash in the XLA/TensorFlow execution path, likely related to shape computation, integer overflow, or invalid buffer planning for the padded tensor.

Reproducer:
import tensorflow as tf
tf.keras.mixed_precision.set_global_policy("mixed_float16")
tf.config.optimizer.set_jit(True)

class MyModel(tf.keras.Model):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.pad = tf.keras.layers.ZeroPadding3D(padding=1610612736)
    def call(self, x):
        return self.pad(x)

model = MyModel()
x = tf.random.uniform((1, 1, 2, 2, 3), dtype=tf.float32)

@tf.function(jit_compile=True)
def compiled_forward(inp):
    return model(inp)

y = compiled_forward(x)

Crash output:
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
exit code: 139

Affected versions: TensorFlow 2.21.0 (tensorflow-cpu). Confirmed reproducible on Ubuntu x86_64.
